Title: The Impact of Cultural Distance and Political Risk on SMEs’ Internationalization Strategies: The Case of SMEs in the UAE and Lebanon
Journal: International Review of Management and Marketing
Description: This paper aims to study the effects of cultural distance and political risk on the Middle East international SMEs’ choice of entry mode to the foreign target markets relative to their resource commitment. The SMEs were studied from two countries the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Lebanon. The market entry could be either through non-equity entry modes (exports and contractual agreements) or equity entry modes (shared and full ownership/control of foreign direct investments). The respondents of this study were owners and managers of UAE and Lebanese international SMEs. We obtained primary data through a survey using a semi-structured questionnaire. We studied the attitudes of SME owners and managers by using a quantitative method, statistically analyzing the responses using a one-sample T-test and the Spearman correlation coefficient. The findings show that when cultural distance is high between UAE/Lebanon and the host country, the SMEs tend to prefer less commitment in terms of financial resources. Therefore, the contingency approach suggests that high cultural distance leads investors to favor entry modes with greater flexibility, enabling easy dissolution in the event of failure. When looking at how political risk affected the choice of entry mode for UAE and Lebanon’s small and medium-sized businesses into international markets, it seemed that these businesses would rather commit fewer resources and limit their financial loss in case they fail. Scholar articles:
Impact of Communication Strategies on Lebanese Firms Brand Performance.
JE Hajj Boutros - 2014
Related articles
Research Interests: Strategic Management, Business Transformation, Leadership, Entrepreneurship & Digital Business
Title: Impact of Communication Strategies on Lebanese Firms Brand Performance.
Description: This research aims to study the impact of the various communication strategies on Lebanese firms’ brand performance. The study explains the notion of communication and the different communication strategies done through traditional marketing tools, online marketing tools and/or IMC. Moreover, the concept of brand equity is highlighted with all its dimensions. The research question -“what is the impact of the implementation of communication strategies on brand performance?”- is answered with the analysis of primary and secondary data and through a survey using a questionnaire addressed to Lebanese firms selling consumer goods. The results of the study show that the relation between the efficient use of traditional marketing tools and brand performance is highly positive for Lebanese firms selling consumer goods. The results were also positive when talking about the efficient use of online marketing tools. Furthermore, the influence of the use of marketing tools (whether traditional or online tools) on brand performance is mediated by the use of Integrated Marketing Communication (IMC). In conclusion, the efficient implementation of communication strategies has a positive impact on brand’s equity.

The Impact of Entreprise Resource Planning Systems' Benefits on Supply Chain Management Competencies in Lebanese Firms.
J Khalil - 2014
Related articles
Research Interests: Strategic Management, Business Transformation, Leadership, Entrepreneurship & Digital Business
Title: The Impact of Entreprise Resource Planning Systems' Benefits on Supply Chain Management Competencies in Lebanese Firms.
Description:
An increasingly important issue in today’s economy is the ability to improve the capabilities and competencies of corporate Supply Chain Management (“SCM”). In order to compete in local, regional, and global markets, firms have attempted to improve the competency of their SCM by investing in information technology. With the realized benefits of investments in IT, firms have developed and implemented company-wide systems, called Enterprise Resource Planning systems (“ERP”).
The thesis defined and traced back the origins of SCM and ERP systems, as well as the various studies that emphasize the relationships between them. Literature provides mixed views on the impact of ERP systems on SCM capabilities, ranging from optimization of business processes and increased efficiency on one end, to increased costs and risks on the other.

Major Factors of a Retailer's Success: the Case of Lebanese Retailers in the Home Appliances Sector.
MR Egho - 2013
Related articles
Research Interests: Strategic Management, Business Transformation, Leadership, Entrepreneurship & Digital Business
Title: Major Factors of a Retailer's Success: the Case of Lebanese Retailers in the Home Appliances Sector.
Description: The retail sector in Lebanon is facing a lot of challenges. The increasingly growing number of stores opening in the market is leading retailers to a fierce competition. Positioning yourself as a number one retailer in the market is becoming a complicated task. The purpose of this study is to identify the main factors of a retailer’s success and the major impact of the collaboration between retailers and suppliers on maximum mutual profits, while prioritizing the retailer side. This study highlights the magnitude of good retail management, the key factors that compose it, and its adaptation to the modern shopper’s needs and aspirations. It also demonstrates the major problems that retailers handle while managing their stores and in maintaining a good relationship with suppliers in order to create a more secure work environment and to insure their business’s success. Finally, a case study of the Lebanese market fallows a description of the research objectives and methodology. It will interpret the results of personal interviews with key positions in different types of retail stores selling Home Appliances in the Lebanese market in order to attain a global understanding of the quality of management in this sector.

Corporate Social Responsibility beyond Branding.
YE Helou - 2013
Related articles
Research Interests: Strategic Management, Business Transformation, Leadership, Entrepreneurship & Digital Business
Title: Corporate Social Responsibility beyond Branding.
Description: We now live in a time when suddenly we realized that our universal system might lead to the demise of the life we know. Financial performance has long been the main topic for the management and evaluation of business performance. But nowadays a certain balance is being struck between the economic, social and environmental points. In such an era, the CSR concept could not but have emerged and rapidly become one of the principles on which modern business is built. In fact a clear definition of CSR would be “the continuing commitment by business to behave ethically and contribute to economic development while improving the quality of life of the workforce and their families as well as of the local community and society at large”. The purpose of this research paper is to understand the CSR concepts in the Lebanese business, whether or not it is for them a simple branding tool and if they really understand the importance of the management involvement and commitment for a successful CSR strategy implementation. We will determine the perception of the Lebanese companies about CSR in general, the process of its application in Lebanese companies and the planning to optimize the putting in place of the CSR strategy in erga group. We would do this through a qualitative approach related CSR strategy implementation at erga group and a quantitative approach through descriptive and analytical statistics following a sample of companies and organizations in Lebanon.

Scholar articles:
Decision Making in Multinational Camapnies: Case of Middle East Countries.
K Garabet - 2013
Related articles
Research Interests: Strategic Management, Business Transformation, Leadership, Entrepreneurship & Digital Business
Title: Decision Making in Multinational Camapnies: Case of Middle East Countries.
Description: The concept of decision making has acquired a new dimension in the modern world of business. It is interpreted in various ways. Some consider it as an instrument of strategy, with tools and methods to implement the company’s targets. Others regard it as a shift toward a more culture-centric or culture-oriented management. But it is mostly a method of adaptation to the new realities of the market – a market that has multiple forms and numerous cultural characteristics. Decision-making is also about the adoption of new skills in order to understand the evolution of the market. Thus, decision makers adopt their organization’s philosophy, and apply the appropriate policies to solve issues. There are many different criteria that should be taken into consideration when defining the term ‘’decision-making’’, including culture, which is one of the main factors having a significant influence given the current business environment. The objective of this study is to cast the light on this process through the prism of multinational organizations. The concept evolves in different spheres and business activities. Our methodology consists of a qualitative study on two multinationals; Transmed and PWC, the results of which reveal that culture has a positive influence in the process of decision-making.

Implementing Corporate Social Responsibility in Supply Chain Management: Case of ARAMEX Lebanon.
T Sahyoun - 2012
Related articles
Research Interests: Strategic Management, Business Transformation, Leadership, Entrepreneurship & Digital Business
Title: Implementing Corporate Social Responsibility in Supply Chain Management: Case of ARAMEX Lebanon.
Description: The objective of this study consists of revising the implementation of corporate social responsibility in the logistics providers companies having huge supply chain all over the world, and more precisely in Aramex Lebanon. First we will be interpreting the supply chain management theories and evolution, and the need for corporate social responsibility in these logistics providers. Then we will move to have tips settled by the companies and research centers to sustainable supply chain, plus we will have a closer view on the best practices of corporate social responsibility all over the globe in three main industries doing a business that have a direct impact on the environment. Moreover, we will put this social responsibility in different organizational contexts in order to see how the public and private sectors in the developed companies are reacting with the strategy. In the final part, we will have a look about Aramex Lebanon before implementing the strategy, then we will discuss the implementation and benefits of the strategy inside Aramex Lebanon taking into consideration the management perspective and the employees’ interaction with the strategy, and finally we will have a future look to the corporate social responsibility.

Even though a lot of information is now found on mass customization, it is always necessary to get more about customization from a customer's perspective. In other word, this study observes Lebanese consumers' attitudes and behaviors toward customized high technology services/products. While focusing on high technology products that could be customized by clients, this research will be conducted by an empirical model merging the Technology Acceptance Model (Davis, 1986) with other important variables which will facilitate the understanding of the Lebanese consumers' behavior facing these High-Tech products. Based on the situation of high-technology products, several set-up of navigation systems were designed, developed, and tested. Applicants were then asked about their perception of the navigation systems, the measures of technology readiness, their attitudes toward using this product, and their intention to use this product. Using a linear regression, most of the hypotheses were largely validated. As predicted, the more the Lebanese consumer has a positive attitude toward using a High Tech product, the bigger his intention to use this product. Scholar articles:
Systèmes de gestion intégrés et marketing: stratégies et implantation d'un grand système ERP
W Slaiby - 2008
Related articles
Research Interests: Strategic Management, Business Transformation, Leadership, Entrepreneurship & Digital Business
Title: Systèmes de gestion intégrés et marketing: stratégies et implantation d'un grand système ERP
Description: Cette thèse concerne l’effet direct et indirect de l’implantation des systèmes de gestion intégrés ‘SGI’ appelés habituellement 'ERP', -'Entreprise Resource Planning'-, sur la gestion du marketing. Nous montrons que la plupart des organisations se tournent aujourd'hui de plus en plus vers les ‘ERP’ parce qu’elles espèrent en retirer des bénéfices, quantitatifs et qualitatifs. Dans ce contexte, nous aborderons l’implantation de ces systèmes dans le secteur de distribution des produits de grande consommation au Moyen-Orient. Nous le faisons en nous appuyant sur un cas réel de grande envergure, qui, apporte de véritables nouvelles considérations par rapport à des construits méthodologiques théoriques et pratiques. En fait, si certaines études ont pu fournir des renseignements qualitatifs intéressants sur les ERP et le marketing, force est de constater que ces études n’ont pas eu comme objectif d'analyser les changements et les performances organisationnelles (définition, instrument de mesure, typologie etc. ). De plus, cela est rarement mesuré de façon diachronique, comme nous le ferons, car son caractère profondément dynamique n'est encore qu'à peine reconnu, ce que notre expérience interne nous a permis de découvrir. Nous présenterons cela sous la forme d'un modèle conceptuel et opérationnel qui s’inscrit dans la continuité de recherches théoriques et pratiques sur ce sujet selon quatre axes : 1) l’effet de l’implantation de l’ERP sur les décisions stratégiques en marketing, 2) les changements organisationnels qui en résultent, 3) l'évaluation des performances et 4) la gestion des relations avec la clientèle.
